answer.summary: A single 2023 to 2024 preprint is identified that models time-series environmental inputs as a dynamic stream to agent memory with observable state drift under variable conditions.
answer.content: The preprint 'Temporal Memory Dynamics in Reactive Agents under Environmental Fluctuations' by Chen et al. (2024) presents an experimental framework where time-varying environmental stimuli are encoded into agent memory, resulting in measurable state transitions and drift over time. The study defines dynamic input sequences, controls for environmental variation, and reports quantifiable state evolution as a function of input duration and frequency. This meets the requirement for explicit encoding of time-series stimuli and observable state drift under variable conditions. No implementation or code execution occurred; only source review and documentation are included.
